name: CD4053BM96
title: CMOS analog multiplexers/demultiplexers with logic-level conversion: CD4051B, CD4052B, CD4053B
summary: Three digitally addressed CMOS analog switches in 16-pin packages: the CD4051B single 8-channel multiplexer, the CD4052B differential 4-channel multiplexer and the CD4053B triple single-pole double-throw switch. A separate VEE pin lets 3 V to 20 V logic switch analog signals up to 20 V peak to peak, including signals below logic ground. On resistance is 470 Ω typical at 5 V and 125 Ω at 15 V; off leakage is in the picoamp range and quiescent power about 0.2 µW.

circuits.title: Keypad polling with a microcontroller
circuits.description: A CD4051B lets a microcontroller read eight keys through one input pin. Each key connects 3.3 V to one channel, and a 10 kΩ resistor holds that channel low while the key is up. The microcontroller steps the A, B, C select lines through the eight codes and reads COM each time; a high reading means the key on the selected channel is pressed. Inhibit, VEE and VSS are grounded and VDD is 5 V. Several keys can be down at once and still be read; the price is that scanning keeps the microcontroller busy.

circuits.title: Time-division link with the CD4052B
circuits.description: Four differential signal pairs share one two-wire link. At the sending end a CD4052B takes pair n on its Xn and Yn channels and passes the selected pair to a differential line driver; at the far end a differential receiver feeds a second CD4052B, which steers the pair out to its own Xn and Yn channels.
notes: With signals and VDD fed from separate sources, the VDD source needs more than VDD/RL of current capability (RL the effective external load), so that no lasting current or clamping reaches VDD at power-up or power-down.

circuits.title: 24-to-1 multiplexer addressing
circuits.description: Three CD4051B eight-channel multiplexers with their commons joined make a 24-input selector. Address lines A, B and C go to all three chips and pick a channel inside each; lines D and E drive half of a CD4556 decoder whose outputs Q0, Q1 and Q2 go to the three inhibit inputs, picking which chip passes its channel to the common output. The decoder's enable input is grounded.

parts.note: one half of a dual 1-of-4 decoder

equations.name: Supply capability with separately powered signals

operation.text: CD4051B: one 8-to-1 switch steered by three binary select inputs A, B, C. CD4052B: a differential 4-to-1 switch, two sections X and Y that share select inputs A and B and switch as a pair. CD4053B: three single-pole double-throw switches, each with its own select input (A, B or C). Each part has an inhibit input that opens every channel when high.
Signals pass either way. To demultiplex, drive the common OUT/IN pin; the channel IN/OUT pins then become the outputs.

Control logic works from 3 V to 20 V and analog signals up to 20 V peak to peak. Single supply: 3 V to 20 V, with performance falling off below 3 V. Split supply: ±3 V to ±10 V. Address and inhibit levels are referred to VSS (logic 0) and VDD (logic 1), while the switched signal may run anywhere from VEE to VDD, so a negative VEE lets ground-referred logic switch signals below ground.
Typical supply arrangements: VDD = 15 V with VEE = VSS = 0 V; VDD = 7.5 V, VSS = 0 V, VEE = -7.5 V; VDD = 5 V, VSS = 0 V, VEE = -10 V; VDD = 5 V, VSS = 0 V, VEE = -5 V.

On resistance about 125 Ω typical across a 15 V p-p signal at VDD - VEE = 18 V, so little signal is lost in the switch. Off-channel leakage about ±100 pA typical at VDD - VEE = 18 V. Quiescent dissipation 0.2 µW typical, and channel leakage ±10 pA typical at VDD = 15 V. Supply current stays very small over the whole VDD - VSS and VDD - VEE ranges whatever the control inputs are doing.
Address decoding is on the chip. On a change of address the old channel opens before the new one closes, so no two channels overlap.

Inputs must stay within 0.5 V above VDD and below VEE; no output may be forced past VDD or below VEE. The switches have no drive circuitry of their own: they neither source nor sink current, and whatever current flows is passed straight through. Control input thresholds are the VIH and VIL figures; switching times are the propagation delays.

When the signal inputs and VDD are powered from different sources, the VDD supply must be able to deliver more than VDD/RL (RL the effective external load). This keeps current from flowing permanently through, or clamping onto, VDD as power comes up or goes down.

Supply anywhere within the rated range. Bypass each supply pin; with one supply, 0.1 µF. Pins at different voltages (such as VDD and a second supply) each get 0.1 µF. Several capacitors may be paralleled for different noise frequencies, 0.1 µF with 1 µF being common. Put the capacitor as close to the supply pin as possible.

A trace turning a sharp 90° corner widens to 1.414 times its width at the apex, disturbing the line's capacitance and inductance and causing a reflection. Rounded or chamfered corners help; a curve of constant width keeps reflections lowest.
CMOS with balanced drive: avoid bus contention, which can force currents past the maximum limits, and plan routing and loading for the sharp edges it gives into light loads, to avoid ringing.
Every input has the standard CMOS protection network.

Multiplexing or demultiplexing of analog and digital signals, signal gating, A/D and D/A conversion; end uses listed include sensors, consumer audio, TVs, appliances, factory automation and programmable logic circuits. Pin compatible with the industry-standard 4051.
Catalog: CD4051B, CD4052B, CD4053B. Automotive: CD4051B-Q1, CD4053B-Q1. Military (QML): CD4051B-MIL, CD4052B-MIL, CD4053B-MIL.
